summary: Documented M3-S01 (two Case ValidationRules — Priority_Required_On_Agent_Save, Origin_Must_Be_Known — with the Bypass_Case_Intake_Validation clause) after step-tester marked it tested. Re-rendered PLAN.md/CLARIFICATIONS.md before and after the status transition; created workbook/05-validation-rules.md (first Section 5 file in the build) with three rows (CWB-VR-001, CWB-VR-002, CWB-VR-003) and appended two Other-Configuration rows (CWB-OTHER-017 package.xml, CWB-OTHER-018 deploy-order.md); minted two new requirement ids (REQ-030 Priority, REQ-031 Origin), continuing from the highest existing (REQ-029), and wrote their traceability.md Matrix rows, a requirement-id-derivation pair, a 'What M3-S01 rests on' section, a Coverage section and a Linter-result section; appended six decisions (D-M3S01-01..06, one per item in deploy-order.md's 'Marked as ungrounded' list) and four open items for the planner (O-M3S01-01..04, including two correction-of-record items against REQ-014 and REQ-015 which this run's own artefacts touch but does not edit); compiled the step's one manual test (W01) into four UAT cases (TC-M3S01-01..04, positive and negative per rule) and four Given/When/Then criteria (AC-030.1/.2, AC-031.1/.2), staged in the session scratchpad and linted clean by both check_uat_case.py and check_ac_format.py. Set the step's status to documented via build_plan.py. A concurrent M3-S02 run (ui, email templates) was building its own artefacts throughout; every shared file was re-read immediately before each write and only M3-S01's own rows and this run's appended entries were touched.
confidence_rationale: Both artefacts produced a workbook row, both new traceability rows carry a real source_req_id (Q5, with Q24 cited in prose for REQ-031) and a verification cell naming both what passed and what the checker does not prove, both requirements' step (M3-S01) is documented, and re-running this pass would replace the same rows rather than duplicate them. Not MEDIUM: no artefact needed judgment to place in a section (validation rules map cleanly to Section 5), no req_id was inferred from an ambiguous field, and the concurrent M3-S02 write surfaced as an orphan-count observation rather than a conflict this run had to resolve.

process_observations.observation: The declared checker's REVIEW rule for a missing blank guard did not fire on either rule, and the step's own fixture fed to it during planning reproduced the documented pass/fail boundary exactly.

Both errorDisplayField values (Priority, Origin) are confirmed present as layoutItems on both Case layouts from M1-S02, so assumption A13's premise now holds concretely for both new rules rather than only in principle.

The step's declared checker test description claims check_validation_rules.py verifies field-token and errorDisplayField resolution; the script has no field inventory and does neither, a gap the owning agent and the tester both independently named.

Six distinct grounding gaps in deploy-order.md's own 'Marked as ungrounded' list were carried forward as decisions rather than resolved, because none can be settled without either a documented Metadata API guarantee or an org validation this build has not run for M3.

The ten-position deploy-order sequence in agents/build-doc-keeper/AGENT.md Step 5 (objects, fields, picklists, record types, layouts, permission sets, sharing, automation, routing, SLA) has no slot named for the validation step type, the same gap workbook/01-objects-and-fields.md already records for BusinessProcess.
Whether these two rules are unbypassable invariants depends on M4-S03's before-save flow being the sole post-save writer of Priority/Origin, and M4-S03 does not exist yet to confirm it against.
M3-S01 is documented; M3-S02 (running) is the remaining M3 step this run observed in flight, and M3-S03/S04/S05 remain pending or blocked before the milestone can be verified.
process_observations.followup_reason: M3-S02 is running and M3-S03 depends on it; advancing the milestone requires those steps built, tested and documented next.

process_observations.observation: check_validation_rules.py's missing field-inventory logic is a repeated, uninstrumented manual check every build reaching a validation step must redo by hand.
process_observations.followup_reason: recorded here as a skill-depth candidate rather than acted on, because deepening a checker script is out of this agent's scope and belongs to the skill's own maintenance path, not a workbook compile.
